title: Dialpad review 2026: Features, pricing, & limitations
summary: An honest Dialpad review for small businesses. What Dialpad does, what it costs, where it shines, and where it falls short.
body_markdown:
Dialpad is an AI-heavy customer communication platform that works best for large sales and support teams. It offers live transcription, call summaries, and AI coaching as an add-on in one system. Small teams that mainly need reliable calling and texting often find it overpriced and overbuilt. Plans start at $15 per user per month, but seat minimums and add-on fees can push costs higher.


This Dialpad review breaks down its VoIP services, AI tools and features, and the pricing and limitations to expect.


##


What is Dialpad?


Dialpad is a[hosted VoIP](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-hosted-voip/) phone system and unified communications platform. That means it supports phone calls, texts, and video meetings over the internet. The base plan offers basic phone features like unlimited calling within your country and to the US and Canada and team messaging. Its AI layer is the main draw: DialpadGPT powers real-time transcription, and every plan includes automated call recaps and searchable voicemail.


While it was originally designed for enterprise brands, Dialpad *does* offer support to smaller businesses. It offers three different products in 2026:


- **Connect:** For general business communication needs
- **Support:** For larger contact and support centers
- **Sell:** For dedicated outbound sales and cold calling


We’re mainly evaluating Dialpad Connect, since it’s the most popular of the three among small and growing businesses. But if you’re interested in exploring other Dialpad products, check out our breakdown of[Dialpad pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-pricing/) .

##


What Dialpad is used for


Most businesses use Dialpad for business calling, texting, and video meetings. They also use its AI call transcripts to help capture and summarize conversations.


The teams that get the most out of Dialpad are sales and support groups that need to collect conversation data. They need live transcriptions, AI call summaries, and real-time coaching to shorten follow-ups and train reps.


This is also why Dialpad is typically a poor fit for a small business. If you’re mostly looking for a shared phone number, you might not use many of Dialpad’s more robust features. You might be paying for expensive contact center tools just to support everyday calling and texting needs.


##


How Dialpad works


Dialpad lets you send calls and texts over the internet instead of a traditional phone line.


First, you install the Dialpad app on a computer, phone, or desk phone. Then an admin user, typically the first person in your business to create a Dialpad account, sets up your phone system from the web portal. This includes configuring settings for phone numbers, interactive voice response or IVR, and call routing. Finally, your Dialpad admin adds new users by sending email invites.


Since Dialpad is a[softphone](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-a-softphone/) , anyone with an internet connection can make and take business calls from any device. That lets every new user on your Dialpad account call, text, and host video meetings on their phone, tablet, or computer.


##


Dialpad AI


Dialpad’s AI features are its biggest claim to fame.


Let’s break down the most popular tools on the Connect plan:


- [DialpadGPT](https://www.dialpad.com/features/dialpad-gpt/) **.** This is a specialized large language model, or LLM, that creates live call transcriptions during each call. That lets you easily search for keywords in calls, meetings, and voicemails. Just keep in mind its best use cases, like CSAT and Scorecards, require upgrades or add-ons.
- **AI recaps.** Summarize calls so you can review them at a glance. You’re also given a list of action items, which can help you decide what next steps to take.
- **Real-time assist.** Offer coaching to reps mid-call with pop-up cards that provide feedback or suggestions. For example, if the AI detects that a rep is talking too fast, it then “pops up” a reminder to slow down and check if the prospect is following along. This is also available as an add-on.
- **Real-time analytics and reporting.** This includes metrics for call volume and rep performance. It also provides live[sentiment analysis](https://www.quo.com/blog/voice-call-sentiment-analysis/) . That way, you can spot unhappy callers early and let a supervisor step in to handle the call.


An important note: Dialpad Connect’s AI tools are *assistive* , not dedicated *AI agents* . They’re designed to help reps manage calls more productively. But they can’t autonomously handle phone calls.


In contrast, Quo’s Sona is an[AI voice agent](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/voice-agent) that answers and handles calls without human help. It lives inside Quo, which works natively with AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT. That way, you can automate more tasks and never miss a call.


##


The good and the bad with Dialpad


First, the good: Dialpad’s AI works for larger businesses and growing teams. It includes AI call recaps and analytics with every plan, unlike alternatives such as[Ooma](https://www.quo.com/blog/ooma-alternatives/) . It offers voice and video conferencing, desk phone support, and local numbers in 50+ countries. Plus, it has a lower entry price compared to some competitors.


So, what are the downsides of Dialpad? Let’s look at several limitations:


- **User minimums.** Dialpad’s base plan only requires one user, but that isn’t the case with the other plans. Upgrading to Pro requires you to purchase a minimum of three seats, even if you don’t have that many users. The Enterprise plan requires a 100-seat minimum. Most Dialpad competitors let you buy the exact number of seats you need, with no user minimums or hidden fees.
- **Video conferencing runs in a separate app.** To host video meetings through Dialpad on laptops and desktops, you’ll need to download a dedicated[Dialpad Meetings app](https://www.dialpad.com/download/#windows) . This means you can’t track all customer conversations in one place — you’ll need to bounce between multiple platforms.
- **Missing call center controls on the Connect plan.** Want features like call barging, monitoring, and whispering? You’ll need to purchase the more expensive[Dialpad Support product](https://www.dialpad.com/pricing/#contact-center) . Prices start at $80 per user per month and don’t include add-ons for AI features like live coaching and scorecards. ******
- **Poor reliability.** Small teams on Dialpad say that reliability can be an issue. Some cite issues like[customer calls going straight to voicemail](https://www.capterra.com/p/190976/Dialpad-Sell/#Capterra___2384383) . Others say that[call transcriptions aren’t accurate](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/64ac20ae068fcf43c4b93ea8) and the desktop and mobile apps can be glitchy. It doesn’t help that[customer support can be slow](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/6a70e7ec6c9ba19511d7f33c) , which means technical issues may stick around for long periods.
- **Weak and confusing international calling.** Enabling international service is a multi-step process. First, an admin user needs to enable the feature in the admin portal. Then you need to add credits or purchase the Global Unlimited Calling add-on, which includes 8,000 international minutes per month per license. There’s no public pricing available for the add-on. Plus, Dialpad doesn’t guarantee delivery of international texts, citing international carrier restrictions.
- **Smaller integration catalog.** Dialpad’s App Marketplace offers a few dozen out-of-the-box integrations, versus a few hundred pre-built integrations for competitors like[RingCentral](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-alternatives/) . Some connections also carry extra costs: custom integrations built through Dialpad’s Professional Services are quoted separately, and certain integrations, including Microsoft Teams, are limited to the pricier Pro and Enterprise plans.
- **Limited SMS and MMS support.** Dialpad includes only[250 outbound texts per user per month](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-sms/) in the US. Anything beyond that will incur additional fees. You also won’t have access to key automations, like scheduled messages or text templates. This can add to your administrative load and increase no-shows, unless you’re willing to work after hours.


For a breakdown of what Dialpad does well versus where it struggles, see our[Dialpad pros and cons](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-pros-and-cons/) list.


##


Dialpad pricing


There are three pricing levels for Dialpad Connect:


- **Standard:** $15 per user per month for unlimited calls within your country and to Canada and the US, one local number per user, text messages, multi-level auto-attendants, visual voicemail, call forwarding, call recording, and up to three ring groups
- **Pro:** $25 per user per month with a three-user minimum for additional numbers, integrations with[Zapier](https://www.quo.com/integrations/zapier) , HubSpot,[Slack](https://www.quo.com/integrations/slack) , Salesforce, and Zendesk, open APIs and webhooks, and up to 25 ring groups
- **Enterprise:** Call for pricing with a 100-user minimum for unlimited ring groups, single sign-on integrations with Azure, Okta, and OneLogin, and phone number extensions


The pricing might seem fair, but Dialpad’s real cost shows up in the fine print.


First, the Standard plan was designed mainly for single users. You can’t purchase additional numbers or extensions without upgrading to the Pro plan. But to upgrade to Pro, you’ll need a minimum of three users. That means, if you’re a team of two, you’ll have to pay for an empty seat to upgrade.


Starting to grow and need more bandwidth? Like additional ring groups, for example? The only way to do that with Dialpad is to purchase the Enterprise plan. There’s no public pricing available, and it requires a minimum of 100 users.


And no matter how much you upgrade, you’ll always pay extra for certain features. For example, internet fax and additional numbers cost extra.

##


What real users say


According to thousands of user reviews, Dialpad falls in “good, not great” territory. On average, it scores 4.26 out of 5 stars across seven major review platforms.


Individual users tend to praise Dialpad’s AI most: live transcription, call recaps, and summaries come up repeatedly. Reactions to the interface are more divided: some find it clean and easy to set up, while others describe confusing setup and buried settings. The most common user complaints are slow customer support, confusing billing, and inconsistent call quality.


Editorial reviewers are split too. Most credit Dialpad’s lower cost per user and its depth of AI features relative to competitors, but scores range widely. PCMag rates it well below most platforms, while Business.com and BusinessNewsDaily score it higher than any user-review site. Common editorial critiques include a glitchy mobile app and setup that gets complicated as configurations grow.


*“Coming from Dialpad, which was extremely difficult to use and hard to find where different settings were located, Quo has done everything I wanted Dialpad to do and has done it better.”* —[Quo user on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/quo-quo/reviews/quo-review-13120506)

##


Who Dialpad is and isn’t for


Dialpad is a better fit for larger sales and support teams that want voice, messaging, and video calling in one place. Enterprises get built-in transcription and analytics across voice and video, with AI coaching available as an add-on. Since you’ll likely have enough seats to clear the plan minimums, you won’t have to worry about paying for empty seats.


Dialpad is a weaker fit for:


- Small teams wanting a simple and reliable[business phone number](https://www.quo.com/blog/get-business-phone-number/)
- Businesses that can’t meet Dialpad’s user minimums
- Teams making large volumes of international calls
- Healthcare teams that need to text patients — Dialpad’s BAA covers its own environment but not SMS to patients outside Dialpad


Does any of the above sound like you? A simpler platform like Quo will likely cost less while offering similar features.

##


Verdict: Is Dialpad worth it?


Dialpad is a decent phone system for sales and support teams that want AI woven into their calling, texting, and video workflows. It comes with desktop, web, and mobile apps for teams that need to stay connected on the go. Reviewers are divided on the interface, though — some find it clean and quick to set up, while others say it’s hard to navigate.


That said, most small businesses find that Dialpad’s structure works against them. With seat minimums and no additional numbers on the base plan, you may feel forced to upgrade before you’re ready. Plus, most of Dialpad’s best features are locked behind a pricier plan or require an entirely separate product. Coupled with the high number of support and billing complaints, it may not be a fit for small and growing teams.


If you’re mainly looking for a system with reliable calling and texting features, Dialpad can be expensive. And if you want a business phone solution that grows alongside your team, you’ll be better served by a Dialpad alternative.


##


Switching away from Dialpad


Decided to move on from Dialpad? The good news is, you can take your numbers with you.


You can port your existing Dialpad numbers to a new provider within one or two weeks. To avoid unnecessary downtime, you just need to keep your Dialpad service active until the port completes.


For the step-by-step mechanics, follow our guide to[porting your numbers out of Dialpad](https://support.quo.com/getting-started/porting/dialpad) .


##


FAQs


****What is Dialpad used for?****


You can use Dialpad for business calling, texting, and video meetings. It also offers AI that transcribes and summarizes conversations. It’s a popular VoIP platform for sales and support teams that want transcripts, analytics, and add-on AI call coaching in one place.


****Is Dialpad better than Zoom Phone?****


That depends on what you need. Dialpad offers built-in AI and voice intelligence on every plan, while Zoom Phone is cheaper and more effective for video meetings. But for a small team that mainly calls and texts customers, both can be more than you need.


****What is a Dialpad meeting?****


Dialpad offers video meetings in a separate app called Dialpad Meetings, which are available on every platform except the web. You can have up to 150 participants on any Dialpad Connect plan. You can also purchase an add-on for Large Meetings to support up to 1,500 participants.


****Is Dialpad good for cold calling?****


Dialpad can work for cold calling if you buy its dedicated outbound product, Dialpad Sell. This lets you access features like power dialing and real-time AI coaching. Keep in mind, the power dialer requires a Salesforce integration, so it’s not a standalone setup. And because it’s a single-line, lightweight dialer, high-volume outbound teams may find it underpowered. Smaller teams may not need a separate sales product on top of their phone plan.


****Is Dialpad HIPAA compliant?****


Yes, Dialpad supports HIPAA compliance. There’s no separate healthcare plan or minimum tier you have to buy. It lets you sign a Business Associate Agreement, or BAA, which you can do from inside the app. Once signed, the BAA covers most Dialpad products, but not all. Notably, it doesn’t cover faxes for PHI or SMS with PHI sent to patients outside Dialpad, so texting patients isn’t covered by default.


****How much does Dialpad cost?****


Dialpad Connect starts at $15 per user per month, billed annually. The Pro plan costs $25 per user per month. Enterprise requires custom pricing. There’s no free tier, but Dialpad *does* offer a 14-day free trial.
